Seminar Title:

Synthesis of copper based chalcogenide thin films-nanostructures hybrid structures for electronic applications

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Physics and Astronomy

Speaker Name:

Somesh Sabat ( Rollno : 521ph2002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

MC-224, Dept. of Physics and Astronomy, NIT Rourkela

Date and Time:

26 Oct 2026 04:00 PM

Contact:

Jyoti Prakash Kar

Abstract:

The growing demand for photodetectors across the globe has drawn significant attention to the growth of semiconducting metal chalcogenide films due to their unique physical, chemical, and optoelectronic properties. In this work, the CuS thin film has been deposited on a flexible PET (polyethylene terephthalate) by a low-cost chemical bath deposition (CBD) method with a variation in molar concentration of precursor, and deposition temperature. Two different doping materials (Mg, and Sn) have been employed in order to systematically tailor the structural, morphological, and optoelectronic properties of CBD-deposited CuS thin films. The mobility of the CuS thin film increases to (39.4 &plusmn 0.8) cm2/(V∙s) with Mg doping concentration of 4%. The annealing treatment of 3% Sn-doped CuS thin film leads to an increase in mobility from (41.4 &plusmn 0.8) cm2/(V∙s) to (87 &plusmn 2) cm2/(V∙s) with an increase in annealing temperature. The hierarchical CuS nanoflowers have been grown on PET by the microwave heating method with a variation of process parameters. The optimized hierarchical CuS nanoflowers grown at 480 W with the precursor concentration of 0.1 M CuSO4, 0.5 M Na2S2O3, and 0.08 M Na2H2EDTA∙2H2O for 20 min possess a high mobility of (104 &plusmn 2) cm2/(V∙s), and a lower resistivity of (2.52 &plusmn 0.05) &times 10-2 &Omega∙cm. The ZnO nanorods, grown by microwave heating, have been optimized with process parameters such as a molar concentration of 0.025 M, microwave power of 640 W, and microwave time of 30 min. The CuS thin film is deposited on ZnO nanorods by the CBD method at 70 &degC to fabricate a heterojunction. The responsivity and specific detectivity of the Al/CuS thin film-ZnO nanorod/Al photodetector are calculated as (53 &plusmn 2) mA/W and (336 &plusmn 7) &times108 Jones, respectively. The responsivity and specific detectivity of the Pt/CuS thin film-ZnO nanorod/Pt photodetector are calculated as (653 &plusmn 7) mA/W and (1680 &plusmn 30) &times 108 Jones, respectively. The Pt/CuS thin film-ZnO nanorod/Pt UV photodetector could be a potential candidate in the field of flexible and wearable electronics.
